title: Miami Claims Top Spot as Georgia, Alabama, Texas Slip in Week 8 Coaches Poll Rankings
body:
A surprise reshuffle has upended the College Football Coaches Poll for the third straight week, with Miami leaping to the top spot while perennial powerhouses Georgia, Alabama and Texas all slipped down the rankings after a chaotic Saturday that saw five top‑10 teams lose. The Hurricanes’ decisive victory over a struggling opponent vaulted them to No. 1, a position they have not held since the 2001 national championship season, while BYU’s dramatic comeback win against Notre Dame vaulted the Cougars into the top five for the first time in program history.  

Georgia, which entered the week at No. 1, fell to No. 4 after a 31‑28 loss to South Carolina that snapped the Bulldogs’ 13‑game winning streak and ended their hopes of an outright SEC East title. Alabama, sitting at No. 3, dropped to No. 5 following a 24‑21 upset by Arkansas, a defeat that exposed lingering inconsistencies on the Crimson Tide’s offensive line. Texas, another top‑ten staple, slipped from No. 5 to No. 9 after a 38‑35 shootout with Oklahoma State left the Longhorns with a vulnerable defense and raised questions about quarterback continuity.  

The Hurricanes’ ascent was anchored by a commanding 42‑14 triumph over a beleaguered opponent, showcasing a balanced attack that blended a potent aerial game with a bruising ground assault. Quarterback Michael Pratt threw for 285 yards and three touchdowns, while running back D’Juan Reed added 112 rushing yards and two scores. Miami’s defense, long considered a work in progress, forced four turnovers and limited its adversary to a single field goal in the second half, reinforcing the narrative that the program has finally aligned its pieces for a legitimate championship run.  

Meanwhile, BYU’s climb into the top five was fueled by an electrifying 31‑28 comeback victory over Notre Dame. Trailing 28‑10 with just over five minutes left, the Cougars engineered a series of quick strikes, highlighted by a 70‑yard touchdown pass from quarterback Jaren Hall and a game‑winning field goal as time expired. The win not only snapped a three‑game losing streak but also signaled that the Cougars can compete with traditional powerhouses on the national stage. Notre Dame, which fell six spots to No. 12, struggled to contain BYU’s aggressive play‑calling and will need to regroup quickly as they approach a critical stretch of conference play.  

The broader implications of this week’s upheaval are significant for the postseason landscape. With five top‑ten teams tasting defeat, the race for conference championships and the coveted College Football Playoff spots has become markedly more fluid. Georgia now faces a must‑win scenario in its remaining SEC matchups to secure a spot in the SEC Championship Game, while Alabama must rely on a strong finish and favorable outcomes in other divisions to remain in playoff contention. Texas, despite its slide, still retains a pathway to the Big 12 Championship if it can string together victories against ranked foes in the coming weeks.  

Looking ahead, the next round of polls will likely reflect the volatility that has defined this season’s middle stretch. Miami’s newfound leadership position places a target on its back, as opponents will intensify their preparations to dethrone the Hurricanes. BYU’s surge adds another contender to the conversation for an at‑large playoff berth, while the traditional powerhouses must demonstrate resilience to reclaim their former standing. As the regular season enters its decisive phase, fans can expect further surprises, and the evolving rankings will continue to shape the narrative of a college football year that refuses to settle into predictability.
